title: Agentic Environment Engineering: A Survey
hook: Agents only get as good as the worlds they practice in. This survey maps the full lifecycle of agent environments — how we model, synthesize, evaluate, and grow them.
key_points: Frames 'environment engineering' as a lifecycle: modeling, synthesis, evaluation, and application of the interactive worlds agents learn in.
Catalogs environments along eight attributes and eight domains, tracing how their capabilities developed.
Distinguishes two synthesis paradigms — symbolic synthesis and neural synthesis — each with matching evaluation methods.
Names four agent-evolution pathways: memory-centric, orchestration-centric, trajectory-centric (offline), and exploration-centric (online).
Points to future directions: Environment-as-a-Service, multi-agent environments, and neural-symbolic environments.
content_html: Environments are the interactive systems LLM agents act in, and they quietly drive how far agent capabilities can evolve — yet, the authors note, the field lacks a systematic account of them. This survey studies agentic environments through an "environment engineering lifecycle": modeling, synthesis, evaluation, and application. It first characterizes representative environments along eight attributes and eight domains, analyzing how their core capabilities developed.
extra_html: For automated environment synthesis, it lays out two paradigms — symbolic and neural — with the evaluation methods that suit each. It then frames agent–environment co-evolution, naming four complementary pathways for how agents improve in dynamic environments: memory-centric experience evolution, orchestration-centric workflow evolution, trajectory-centric offline evolution, and exploration-centric online evolution, alongside three styles of environment evolution (neural-driven, difficulty-driven, scaling-driven). It closes on open directions like Environment-as-a-Service, multi-agent environments, and neural-symbolic environments. As a survey it's a good orientation card: a map of why "the environment" is becoming a first-class design surface for agents, rather than a single new result.

related.title: EvoArena: Testing Agents in Environments That Keep Changing
related.hook: Most agent benchmarks freeze the world. EvoArena makes the environment keep updating beneath the agent — and finds today's agents crack, averaging under 40%.

related.title: Harness-1: RL for Search Agents with State-Externalizing Harnesses
related.hook: Stop making the policy remember everything. Harness-1 moves a search agent's bookkeeping into the environment, so RL only has to learn the decisions that matter.

flashcards.back_html: Modeling, synthesis, evaluation, and application of the interactive environments in which agents learn and act.

flashcards.prompt: Which two environment-synthesis paradigms does the survey distinguish?
flashcards.explanation_html: The survey separates automated environment synthesis into symbolic and neural paradigms, each paired with its own evaluation methods.

flashcards.prompt: Name two of the four agent-evolution pathways the survey identifies.
flashcards.back_html: Any two of: memory-centric experience evolution, orchestration-centric workflow evolution, trajectory-centric offline evolution, and exploration-centric online evolution.
